# Project Memory

## plan-005: Prompt Type Comparison (2026-05-15)

### Three-way comparison: continuation vs elaboration vs inspired_rewriting

Model: Pythia-2.8B, 1000 seeds (995 valid), 5 depths (0–4), reference model Pythia-410M features.

#### Chain Retention (d4/d0)

| Prompt Type | Records | d0 | d1 | d2 | d3 | d4 | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| continuation | 4620 | 995 | 992 | 932 | 874 | 827 | **83.1%** |
| elaboration | 4946 | 995 | 995 | 989 | 986 | 981 | **98.6%** |
| inspired_rewriting | 4827 | 995 | 995 | 959 | 944 | 934 | **93.9%** |

Continuation loses ~17% of chains by depth 4; elaboration loses only 1.4%.

#### Depth Discriminability (XGBoost, 3-class: gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+)

| Prompt Type | Within-type CV F1 | LOPTO F1 (cross-type transfer) |
|---|---|---|
| continuation | **0.781** ± 0.012 | 0.762 |
| elaboration | 0.730 ± 0.011 | 0.762 |
| inspired_rewriting | 0.737 ± 0.011 | 0.733 |

Continuation has highest within-type discriminability. Cross-type transfer (LOPTO) shows continuation and elaboration are similarly classifiable when trained on the other two types.

#### Feature Drift (d0 → d4 relative change)

| Feature | continuation | elaboration | rewriting |
|---|---|---|---|
| entropy_mean | **−55.7%** | −47.1% | −47.7% |
| ttr | −60.7% | −64.1% | −61.8% |
| hapax_ratio | −74.0% | **−82.8%** | −80.0% |

All three types show large lexical diversity collapse (ttr, hapax_ratio). Continuation has the strongest entropy_mean decay, aligning with its higher discriminability.

#### Key Findings
1. **Retention–discriminability tradeoff**: Elaboration preserves almost all chains (98.6%) but has weakest depth signal (F1=0.730). Continuation loses more chains but the surviving samples carry stronger depth fingerprints (F1=0.781).
2. **Cross-type signal is shared**: LOPTO F1 ~0.75 means a classifier trained on two prompt types transfers reasonably to the third. The depth signal is not prompt-type-specific.
3. **Lexical features dominate drift**: ttr and hapax_ratio show 60–83% collapse across all types, making them the most reliable depth indicators regardless of prompt type.
